title: The Electric Trucking Market’s Record Rise: Three Things to Know | BloombergNEF
gist: BloombergNEF reports global medium- and heavy-duty electric truck sales hit a record 158,000 in 1H 2026 (+75% YoY), over 90% in China where e-trucks are ~20% of truck sales, while Europe reaches 5.5% and the US stalls. Megawatt charging economics hinge on utilization, and financiers are shifting to underwriting e-trucks against contracted freight operations rather than uncertain residual values.

insights.claim: Global sales of medium- and heavy-duty electric trucks reached a record 158,000 vehicles in the first half of 2026, up 75% year over year, and practically all were battery-electric.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Trucks are becoming the next major electrification growth vector, with knock-on demand for batteries and power.
insights.quote: Global sales of medium- and heavy-duty electric trucks reached a record 158,000 vehicles in the first half of 2026

insights.claim: BloombergNEF frames trucks as the new growth story in road transport electrification, with far-reaching implications for electricity demand, battery demand, freight costs and fleet financing.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Investors in batteries, utilities, logistics and lenders should treat truck electrification as a cross-sector demand driver.
insights.quote: Trucks are the new growth story in road transport electrification

insights.claim: Battery-electric technology, not hydrogen or other alternatives, accounts for practically all medium- and heavy-duty electric truck sales as of the first half of 2026.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: The commercial-vehicle drivetrain race is being won by batteries in practice, favoring battery supply chains.

themes.theme: China dominance, Europe uptake, US stall

insights.claim: More than nine out of ten electric trucks sold globally in the first half of 2026 were sold in China, supported by strong policies and an extensive battery supply chain.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: China's policy plus battery supply chain advantage translates directly into commercial-vehicle market dominance.
insights.quote: More than nine out of 10 electric trucks sold globally in the first half of 2026 were in China
insights.locator: China dominates, but growth is spreading

insights.claim: Continuous market growth has pushed electric trucks to about 20% of total truck sales in China.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A 20% share signals e-trucks are past early adoption in the largest truck market, pressuring diesel truck and fuel demand.
insights.quote: Continuous market growth has pushed electric trucks to about 20% of total truck sales.
insights.locator: China dominates, but growth is spreading

insights.claim: Electric truck sales shares in Norway and Switzerland are even higher than in China, and in Denmark, the Netherlands and Sweden they exceeded 10% of total truck volumes.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Smaller European markets demonstrate the adoption path that larger markets could follow.
insights.quote: sales shares are even higher in Norway and Switzerland
insights.locator: China remains by far the world's largest

insights.claim: Electric trucks accounted for 5.5% of Europe's total truck sales in the first half of 2026, helped by manufacturers launching new models and electric truck prices beginning to fall.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Falling prices and new model launches suggest Europe's share is set to expand from a low base.
insights.quote: Electric trucks accounted for 5.5% of Europe’s total truck sales in the first half of 2026
insights.locator: China remains by far the world's largest

insights.claim: The US battery-electric truck market has slowed to a near standstill because of policy and cost headwinds.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: US e-truck exposure faces near-term volume risk relative to China and Europe.
insights.quote: the US battery-electric truck market has slowed to a near standstill

insights.claim: Industry participants interviewed by BNEF say Tesla's Semi appears competitively priced at between $250,000 and $300,000 per vehicle.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Pricing data point relevant to Tesla's commercial-vehicle prospects and diesel truck OEM competition.
insights.quote: Tesla’s Semi appears to be priced competitively, at between $250,000 and $300,000 per vehicle

insights.claim: BNEF calculations suggest the Tesla Semi's pricing could already allow it to undercut the total cost of ownership of equivalent diesel trucks in some duty cycles, depending on charging costs.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: TCO parity without subsidies could reopen US e-truck demand despite policy headwinds; charging cost is the swing factor.

insights.claim: Long-haul battery-electric trucking depends on adequate high-power charging infrastructure to quickly top up large truck batteries, and such stations face cost and grid-connection hurdles.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Charging and grid-connection bottlenecks are a gating factor for long-haul adoption and an opportunity for infrastructure builders.
insights.quote: Long-haul battery-electric trucking depends on adequate high-power charging infrastructure

insights.claim: Despite cost and grid hurdles, operators continue to build high-power truck charging stations in Europe, China and the US.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Charging buildout is proceeding across all three major markets, supporting equipment and grid-connection demand.

insights.claim: In Europe, truck charging stations are being developed along freight routes and increasingly sited beside existing logistics infrastructure such as highway truck stops.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Truck-stop owners and logistics real estate gain optionality as charging hosts.
insights.quote: increasingly located beside existing logistics infrastructure, such as highway truck stops

insights.claim: EU deployment targets under the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) are accelerating construction of truck charging stations.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Regulatory mandates provide a demand floor for European charging infrastructure investment.
insights.quote: Deployment targets set by the European Union through its Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) are also accelerating construction.

insights.claim: European truck charging network growth has not yet eliminated patchy and concentrated coverage across countries and regions where early adopters operate.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Coverage gaps remain a constraint on fleet adoption and an unfilled investment opportunity.
insights.quote: network growth has yet to eliminate patchy and concentrated coverage

insights.claim: Megawatt-scale charging operators would need to charge roughly $0.10 to $0.22 per kilowatt-hour on top of the cost of electricity to recover their investment, with economics improving as station utilization rises.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Utilization is the key driver of charging-station returns; the margin range sets a benchmark for e-truck TCO.
insights.quote: operators would need to charge roughly $0.10 to $0.22 per kilowatt-hour to recover their investment

insights.claim: Utilization currently varies widely among megawatt truck charging stations, which makes charging-station returns uneven.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Investors should diligence site-level utilization rather than assume network-average returns.
insights.quote: For now, however, utilization varies widely among stations.

insights.claim: Incumbent and startup companies are developing new ways to finance and operate electric truck fleets, including in the US despite its relatively small electric truck market.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Financing innovation is a leading indicator that capital is positioning for e-truck scale even where sales lag.
insights.locator: As the electric truck market grows

insights.claim: BNEF interviews indicate electric truck financing transactions are increasingly underwritten against the truck's contracted transport operation rather than its resale value alone.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A shift from asset-based to contract-based underwriting changes the credit risk profile and opens e-truck finance to infrastructure-style investors.
insights.quote: financing transactions are increasingly underwritten against the truck’s contracted transport operation, rather than its resale value alone

insights.claim: Contract-backed instruments being used for electric trucks are standard financial tools but have been relatively unused in diesel truck financing.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Truck electrification is reshaping fleet finance practices, not just drivetrains.
insights.quote: they have been relatively unused in diesel truck financing

insights.claim: Financiers, fleet owners and shippers adopt contract-backed instruments to counteract wide variability in electric truck residual values caused by uncertainty around battery degradation.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Residual-value uncertainty from battery degradation is a core risk that structured finance is designed to neutralize.
insights.quote: wide variability in electric truck residual values due to uncertainty around battery degradation

insights.claim: These e-truck financing transactions rely on relatively long-term freight contracts and, in regions with carbon schemes, on the value of emissions reductions, making them attractive to large corporate shippers and major investors.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Carbon pricing and long-term freight contracts turn e-truck fleets into bankable, yield-like assets for large investors.
insights.quote: Both features make them attractive to large corporate shippers and major investors.
